source.citation: Krutyanskiy et al., Telecom-Wavelength Quantum Repeater Node Based on a Trapped-Ion Processor, Physical Review Letters 130, 213601 (2023)
source.parameter_location: main text enhanced-node projection and Supplementary Sections IV A--B

validity.distance_semantics: distance between neighboring ion nodes; the photonic Bell station is at the midpoint
validity.route_scope: near-future author projection; 17 such nodes and the complete 800 km chain were not demonstrated

hardware.resource_semantics: the source's 17-node model uses two-ion nodes; no unbounded memory-bank assumption

rate_model.published_validation_target: 16 links x 50 km gives T_tot=0.71 s (1.4 Hz)
rate_model.approximation_uncertainty: the source states that the inherited nesting expression is approximate to within a factor 1.5

state_model.published_validation_target: 16 links give final Bell fidelity 0.61 when memory decoherence is neglected under tau >> 0.7 s
state_model.elementary_channel: phase-error Bell mixture from Supplementary Eqs. S13--S14
state_model.local_swap_channel: single-output-qubit depolarizing map from Supplementary Eq. S15

storage_decoherence_model.coherence_time_definition: enhanced-node Gaussian memory parameter used by the source's separate one-repeater secret-key-rate model
storage_decoherence_model.source: Supplementary Section IV B parameter vector

memory_model.decay_semantics: the spin-qubit memory has no natural spontaneous-decay loss in the node protocol
memory_model.long_chain_warning: the source's 800 km fidelity prediction assumes tau much greater than 0.7 s and separately says tens-of-seconds memories should be possible; 0.63 s does not satisfy that asymptotic condition and is retained as the conservative executable parameter

controller_model.scheduling: parallel adjacent-link generation, storage of the first success, and balanced nested local deterministic Bell swapping

notes: This is the paper authors' enhanced-node projection, not a demonstrated system. P_link^0=0.21 and all three state-operation fidelities of 0.99 are author-selected improvement targets supported by cited component directions. The active 0.63 s memory value comes from the paper's separate enhanced-node SKR calculation; the model therefore reports when service time is not safely below coherence time instead of silently assuming an ideal memory.
